title: Eval ensemble and triggerable rollback policy for cost-driven config changes
creator: Evan Cole
description:
Goal: Build a low-risk, broadly applicable evaluation and rollback system that validates batching/caching/quantization recommendations before they are applied live. The focus is on combining multiple automated quality signals into a single decision score, surfacing targeted human spot-checks for borderline changes, and providing a triggerable, reversible rollback policy tied to observable quality regressions.

Why: Recent cost-tuning experiments yield measurable token-cost savings but occasionally introduce subtle semantic regressions for small customer segments. Purely automated thresholds lead to false positives/negatives; purely manual review is slow. We need a reproducible, auditable harness that balances speed, coverage, and safety for config rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) An eval-ensemble service that computes a composite quality score for a candidate config change using: embedding-similarity, n-gram overlap, calibrated LM confidence deltas, and task-specific heuristics.
2) A configurable thresholding policy with three bands (accept, review, reject) and pluggable weights.
3) A human spot-check workflow for 'review' band changes that integrates with the Console QA queue.
4) Shadow-run capability: candidate configs can be routed to X% of traffic in shadow mode for 72 hours with metric collection.
5) A rollback controller that can be triggered automatically when composite score drop exceeds delta and is sustained for configurable window, or manually via Console.
6) End-to-end tests and a dashboard that surfaces per-model, per-route quality deltas and cost savings estimates.
implementation_notes:
Architecture sketch: small microservice (eval-ensemble) subscribes to candidate config events; it spins up an ephemeral job that samples representative requests (via recent traffic traces or synthetic prompts), runs inference with baseline and candidate configs, computes metrics, and emits a unified report. Metrics include: embedding cosine similarity (sentence-transformer on outputs), semantic entailment score (zero-shot NLI model), token-level divergence, latency distribution, and downstream task-specific scores (where available).

Decision policy: configurable YAML defining metric weights and band thresholds. Default conservative weights prioritize semantic-preservation over cost. Human-in-the-loop: when composite score falls in review band, the system opens a Console QA task linking to a small shuffled sample of baseline vs candidate outputs with blind labels for reviewers.

Safety-first rollout: default rollout is shadow -> canary (1%) -> ramp (10/50/100) with automatic hold/rollback conditions defined on composite score delta and customer-impact tags.
test_plan:
Unit tests for metric calculators, integration tests for the shadow routing path, and end-to-end tests that: (a) generate synthetic regressions to validate automatic rollback triggers, (b) validate no-false-positives on benign cost reductions, and (c) exercise human-review flow. Add CI job to run a smoke-eval on each release that verifies the ensemble outputs stable scores for canonical reference anchors.

Acceptance tests will include seeded scenarios: paraphrase-preserving compression (should pass), factual hallucination injection (should reject), and latency-only improvements with no quality regression (should accept).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement core eval-ensemble service and metric primitives, expose a dry-run API. Phase 2 (3 weeks): integrate with shadow routing and Console QA tasks, implement threshold policy editor. Phase 3 (2 weeks): implement automatic rollback controller and dashboard; run internal dogfood on non-production partitions for one month. Default config: run recommendations through the harness for 72h shadow with 5% sampled traffic before any canary. Rollback policy: automatic rollback if composite quality drop > 6% sustained over 3-hour window and corroborated by at least one task-specific metric drop. Manual rollback can be triggered immediately from Console with a 1-click action.
